column1: # Translation collisions that have been LOOKED AT, for scripts/check-1170-translation-collisions.py.
# A collision is a pair of rows `A -> B` and `B -> C`, both real moves, in the tables
# `crates/er-game-base/build.rs` emits. Resolving A once gives B, which is right; resolving the
# result AGAIN gives C, which is wrong -- and it is wrong SILENTLY, because the table cannot tell
# a destination from a source when both are just addresses. It bit once already: `native_submit`
# 0x7ac890 -> 0x7ad710 through `register_shared_hook`, which handed the resolved address to the
# product's union register, which resolved again.
# THIS IS NOT AN EXCUSE LIST. Every line here is printed in full on every run, and the gate fails
# on any collision that is NOT here, or on a recorded one that reaches a table it did not reach
# before. It exists because the three below are facts about two shipped images that this gate is
# not permitted to edit away, and a gate that is red on arrival gets deleted rather than fixed.
# TO CLEAR A LINE: delete the offending row from the ledger and delete the line here. `--strict`
# ignores this file entirely and is the mode to run once they are gone.
# HISTORY OF THIS FILE'S OWN ADVICE, because it has been wrong twice and both times in the
# direction that destroys something:
#   (1) Until 2026-08-30 all three notes ended "the row carries no feature: delete it from both
#       ledgers." That came from a test which searched for `const NAME: usize = 0x<addr>;` and read
#       its own silence as proof of absence. The same test called 0xb0d400 unclaimed while it was
#       declared `MenuJobWait = 0x00b0d400` inside `#[repr(u32)] pub enum MenuTraceRva`, with live
#       uses on the autoload path.
#   (2) The correction then over-swung. The notes were rewritten to say NOT PROVEN because four
#       declarations in `crates/` could not be evaluated. Those four are now evaluated and were
#       never addresses -- `SP_EFFECT_PARAM_INDEX` is a param row index of 15,
#       `CHR_ASM_UNKD4_OFFSET`/`CHR_ASM_UNKD8_OFFSET` are struct offsets 0xd4/0xd8, and
#       `CHR_ASM_ENTRY_COUNT` is a count of 22, each matching an independently documented meaning.
#       The residue that could hold a `.text` RVA is now EMPTY for all three addresses, so the
#       answer today is PROVEN unclaimed, and the NOT-PROVEN wording below was stale.
# WHAT "PROVEN UNCLAIMED" DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It means nothing in `crates/` DECLARES the
# address and no bare literal of it occurs in code. It does NOT mean the address is unreachable:
# a value can be computed from another constant, read out of a live vtable or recovered from a
# call site, and `docs/recon/rva-1170-observed-refusals.txt` exists precisely because 42 of the 54
# addresses the running game asked for on 2026-08-29 were invisible to a declaration scan. Nor is
# a wrong deletion here recoverable from a log: once row B is gone its source is a destination
# that no row claims as a source, `already_translated_in` takes it, and the resolver hands the
# address back UNTRANSLATED with no refusal and no log line -- and on 1.17 that address is a
# different function. The gate computes and prints that per row (`deletion_failure_mode`).
# WHAT SETTLED ALL THREE, 2026-08-30, was a RUN and not a scan. The evidence is in each note:
# every appearance of these addresses in every DLL log is as some other row's translated OUTPUT,
# never as a first request, and each is immediately re-resolved by a hook API. So the collisions
# are NOT inert -- three product detours are being installed on the wrong function right now, and
# each feature's own log line reports the address it MEANT rather than the one it got.
# THE PRIMARY FIX IS THE CALL SITE, NOT THIS FILE. `MhHook::new` and `register_union_hook` resolve
# internally, so a caller that does `game_rva(RVA)` and hands them the RESULT resolves twice. The
# three call sites are named in the notes. Retiring row B is a second, independent mitigation that
# also happens to make these three double resolves idempotent; it is recommended AFTER the call
# sites are fixed and a run confirms no first request for the address, and nobody has executed it.
# THE CARRY, 2026-10-20. The tables hold 1.17.0 destinations; the runtime carries each one to the
# running build before handing it out (`carry_mapped_rva`: identity on 1.17.0, +0x70 above 0xafefe9
# in .text on 1.17.1, that plus docs/recon/carry-1171-to-1172.tsv on 2.7.2.0), and a second resolve
# looks the CARRIED address up as a 1.16.2 source. So the gate scans every build, the collision
# address and second destination below are in the running build's coordinates, and the `builds`
# column names where each one exists. A collision reaching a build it is not recorded on fails the
# run like a new route does. Status of the call sites as of this date: every one of the three
# 2026-08-30 call sites now passes `game_rva_for_hook` (unresolved) to the hook API, so the
# "RECOMMENDED, NOT EXECUTED" in their notes has since been executed; the rows themselves remain.
# first source
